purpose: Test the Phase 3 conversion gate (5-reviewer stack) catches the right things on real sales letter drafts. Compare iteration N (3 reviewers) vs iteration N+1 (5 reviewers including wired-in eval-halbert + eval-sales-letter).

evals.name: neezanizam-v4-firsttime
evals.prompt: Run sales-letter-method Phase 3 conversion gate on this draft. Use the brand context at clients/neezanizam/_brand/. Return all reviewer outputs + synthesized priority fix stack.
evals.expected_output: 5 reviewer reports + synthesizer's ranked Priority Fix Stack. Must catch: mechanism naming conflict (No-Viewings-First Method vs RAM/SPOT in offer.md), audience mismatch (letter targets first-time vs brand targets HDB upgraders), 30-min vs 60-min consult mismatch, placeholder still visible, weasel words (properly, full picture, structural gap, plain English).

evals.prompt: Run sales-letter-method Phase 3 conversion gate on this draft. Use the brand context at <client>/_brand/. Return all reviewer outputs + synthesized priority fix stack.

assertions_to_add_during_grading.description: Output mentions both 'No-Viewings-First Method' AND 'RAM/SPOT' (or current brand mechanism name), explicitly flagging the conflict. Pre-wiring: only eval-sales-letter caught this. Post-wiring: still only eval-sales-letter — but it's now part of Phase 3.
Output flags discrepancy between letter's stated audience and brand docs' stated audience (first-time private buyers vs HDB upgraders).
Output flags at least 3 of these weasels: 'properly', 'full picture', 'plain English', 'structural gap'. Pre-wiring: copy-chief missed all. Post-wiring: eval-halbert catches all 4.
assertions_to_add_during_grading.check: count >= 3 of ['properly', 'full picture', 'plain English', 'structural gap'] flagged with critique

assertions_to_add_during_grading.description: Output flags the '[INSERT: first-timer cohort number]' placeholder in the draft as a ship-blocker.
Synthesizer output has a decisive verdict (SHIP / HOLD / REWRITE), not 'mostly good' hedging.
assertions_to_add_during_grading.check: regex at top of synthesized output: 'SHIP|HOLD|REWRITE|KILL IT|FIX IT|MAIL IT'

assertions_to_add_during_grading.description: eval-halbert's output reads in Halbert's voice (kitchen-table, racetrack metaphors, fatherly bluntness) — not generic 'elite DR strategist' prose. Judge: does this read like Halbert wrote it, or like a consultant?
assertions_to_add_during_grading.check: judge subagent reads eval-halbert output + Halbert reference letters (Boron Letters style) + verdicts pass/fail with evidence

assertions_to_add_during_grading.description: Every flagged finding includes (a) a verbatim quote from the draft AND (b) a specific rewrite or replacement. No abstract 'make it stronger' feedback.
assertions_to_add_during_grading.check: judge subagent samples 5 findings per reviewer and pass/fails based on quote + rewrite presence

assertions_to_add_during_grading.description: Reviewers do NOT flag lines that the operator has explicitly marked as 'working' in the draft's Reviewer Note. False-positive on a strong line indicates the reviewer is over-flagging.
assertions_to_add_during_grading.check: judge cross-references reviewer flags against Reviewer Note section of the draft

iteration_protocol.iteration_1_baseline: Current Phase 3 (3 reviewers: buyer-lens, copy-chief, self-contained). Run all 3 evals. Grade. Save to workspace/iteration-1/.
iteration_protocol.iteration_2_wired: Phase 3 with eval-halbert + eval-sales-letter wired in (5 reviewers). Run all 3 evals. Grade. Save to workspace/iteration-2/.
iteration_protocol.compare: Use skill-creator's eval-viewer with --previous-workspace pointing at iteration-1. Look for: assertion delta (which got caught in iter-2 that wasn't caught in iter-1), cost delta (~+$0.40 per eval), false-positive delta (any new over-flagging).
iteration_protocol.decision_gate: If iteration-2 catches mechanism naming conflict + audience mismatch + ≥3 weasel words AND iteration-1 missed them, keep the wiring. If iteration-2 introduces false positives without commensurate finding gains, revert.
